reuse.why: Extends the existing isMonthWideCategory selector and the existing getBudgetData/getAverageCategories queries rather than adding per-action checks; setZero gets its own inline query instead of a shared category-query helper.

duplication.why: The template predicate is defined once as HAS_BUDGET_TEMPLATE_SQL and spliced into all three queries; the only near-repeat is setZero's new inline SELECT, which mirrors getAverageCategories except for its LEFT JOIN (a real difference that keeps orphan categories).

placement.why: The rule lives in the month-wide selection function in budget/actions.ts, where the tree already decides which categories month-wide actions write.

scope.why: Changes are limited to the selector, its data queries, the five month-wide call sites and matching tests.

maintainability.why: One predicate and one SQL fragment make the rule easy to change; the removal of the includeHidden option is clean, though the SQL definition of a saved template is a second notion of templates separate from goal-template.ts parsing.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All month-wide actions still go through isMonthWideCategory.

disguised_duplication.where: No duplicated logic is disguised; setZero's query differs from getAverageCategories by a deliberate join type.

one_place.where: isMonthWideCategory in budget/actions.ts (hidden, group hidden, has_budget_template), fed by the shared HAS_BUDGET_TEMPLATE_SQL fragment used in every month-wide query.
